Henrik Ibsen, Ghosts, translated by William Archer.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/henrik-ibsen/ghosts/william-archer

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Henrik Ibsen, an author, died 1906.
- William Archer, an annotator, translator and writer of the introduction, died 1924.

First publication of the text used: 1911 (SE colophon: 'Ghosts was published in 1881 by Henrik Ibsen. It was translated from Norwegian in 1911 by William Archer.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1911. The edition's own statement of rights (quoted below) says the text is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin: the facts do not name the country of first publication. Every person named above died in 1924 or earlier, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon (quoted above): publication year 1911.
- Wikidata Q36661 (Henrik Ibsen), P570 = 1906-05-23
- Wikidata Q1382278 (William Archer), P570 = 1924-12-27
